title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Rényi Entropies Estimation
authors: Zongxing Xiong, Chengshen Gao, Lvzhou Li
abstract: Entropy estimation of discrete probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistical inference and quantum property estimation. In this paper, we study the problem of estimating Rényi entropy $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ for any distribution $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i=1}^n$ given its purified quantum query-access. For non-integer $α> 1$, our algorithm estimates $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ to within additive error $ε$ using only $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{\max\{1/2,1-1/α\}}/ε\big)$ queries, which improves the best known upper bound for dependence on both $n$ and $1/ε$. For $0<α<1$, our algorithm has query complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{1/(2α)}/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$, which improves the dependence on $1/ε$ of the current best upper bound without incresing its $n$ dependence. Our approach adapts the multi-level estimation framework to relative approximation of the power sums and leverage binary search to remove the requirement of prior knowledge of them. We also strengthen the precision-dependent lower bound to $Ω\big(1/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$ for $0<α<1$, which identifies the optimal precision dependence of our algorithm.
summary: This paper presents improved quantum algorithms for estimating Rényi entropies using quantum query access. By adapting a multi-level estimation framework, the authors achieve better query complexity bounds for both $\alpha > 1$ and $0 < \alpha < 1$. The work establishes optimal precision dependencies by matching the derived upper bounds with strong lower bounds.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental problem of estimating the Rényi entropy $H_\alpha(p)$ for a discrete probability distribution $p$ using quantum query access.
main_result: They derive improved upper bounds and establish optimal lower bounds for the quantum query complexity required for this estimation, particularly for non-integer $\alpha$.
method: The approach adapts a multi-level estimation framework, utilizing quantum tools like Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) and polynomial approximations, to estimate the required power sums.
model_or_system: The problem is modeled using purified quantum query-access to the distribution $p$, involving unitaries $U_p$ and projected unitary encodings.
key_observables: Rényi entropy $H_\alpha(p)$ and the associated power sum $P_\alpha(p) = \sum p_i^\alpha$.
important_parameters: The accuracy $\epsilon$ and the entropy parameter $\alpha$ (covering regimes $\alpha > 1$ and $0 < \alpha < 1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on adapting the multi-level framework to handle relative approximation requirements for the power sums.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general quantum tools (QSVT, QAE) to the specific multi-level framework, first addressing the $\alpha > 1$ case, and then outlining the approach for $0 < \alpha < 1$, culminating in complexity analysis and lower bound proofs.
why_interesting: The development of quantum algorithms for estimating fundamental statistical properties like entropy is crucial for quantum characterization of quantum states and quantum resources.
